profile.headline: AI/ML Software Engineer | Scientific Software Architecture | Production AI/ML Systems | Modeling & Simulation
profile.summary:
I am an AI/ML software engineer and researcher working at the intersection of intelligent systems, modeling and simulation, software architecture, and human-autonomy teaming.
 
My path into technology has been unconventional. I served as an airborne infantryman and paratrooper with A Troop, 5th Squadron, 73rd Cavalry Regiment, the reconnaissance, surveillance, and target-acquisition element of the 3rd Brigade Combat Team, 82nd Airborne Division. I deployed to Iraq in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom and participated in combat operations during 2008 and 2009.
 
After leaving the Army, I spent several years as a touring and session bassist. I performed at SXSW three times with two different artists, recorded with multiple artists, and designed a live playback and in-ear monitoring system for stage performance. That work strengthened many of the same abilities I now apply to engineering: systems thinking, disciplined preparation, real-time troubleshooting, and collaboration under pressure.
 
I later completed a B.S. in Computer Science, a mathematics minor, and an M.S. in Computer Science, and I am now pursuing a PhD in Computer Science and Engineering. My master’s research explored counterfactual knowledge distillation for more robust, efficient, and interpretable natural-language inference. My current research examines trust-aware adaptive autonomy and human-machine teaming.
 
Professionally, I develop software supporting defense modeling and simulation, with experience spanning AI/ML, MATLAB, Python, CI/CD, software architecture, distributed systems, performance optimization, technical documentation, and scientific computing.
 
I am especially interested in intelligent systems that must perform outside the laboratory, especially systems that need to be understandable, dependable, computationally practical, and useful to the people relying on them.

positions.title: AI/ML Software Engineer
positions.description:
Develop and modernize mission-focused scientific software supporting modeling, simulation, and algorithm integration across connected and air-gapped environments.
 
 - Helped transform a tightly coupled MATLAB legacy application into a modular, SOLID-based architecture using interfaces, dependency injection, factories, strategy patterns, and separation of algorithms from orchestration.
 - Partner with scientists and physicists to integrate computational algorithms into production software while balancing correctness, performance, maintainability, and testability.
 - Designed and maintain a GitLab CI/CD platform coordinating runners with two remote compute servers and supporting four concurrent, load-balanced jobs.
 - Built merge-request quality gates that run 900+ unit tests, smoke-test two application modes, validate outputs, and block unverified changes from merging.
 - Developed a nightly workflow for testing, coverage analysis, extended validation, container builds, registry publication, and HTML/email status reports with direct links to failed jobs.
 - Improved application and test performance through multiprocessing, caching, parallel execution, and compute-resource load balancing.
 - Established module-level performance metrics to identify bottlenecks and guide optimization.
 - Introduced standardized Doxygen documentation with automated publication to GitLab Pages and Confluence.
 - Designed CI behavior for low-side and classified air-gapped deployments using private package mirrors and environment-specific execution paths.
 - Review code and mentor engineers and scientists in architecture, testing, CI/CD, performance, and software-engineering practices.
 - Support production-ready delivery every two-week sprint and program-increment releases within a Scaled Agile Release Train.
 - Integrated ChatGPT and Claude Code into approved workflows for testing, documentation, refactoring, troubleshooting, and developer productivity.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Supported software engineering, machine-learning analysis, and internal application development for defense modeling and simulation programs.
 
 - Developed machine-learning methods to compare proprietary simulation software with U.S. Air Force modeling and simulation tools while preserving strict security and confidentiality requirements.
 - Worked with AFSIM, COSMOS, Galaxy, Dakota, Python, Bash, AWS, and scientific-computing workflows to analyze software capabilities and appropriate use cases.
 - Built data-processing and comparative-analysis pipelines to support technical decision-making and software evaluation.
 - Contributed to a web application for analyzing project-management data using Python, Flask, MongoDB, and JavaScript.
 - Collaborated with engineers and stakeholders to translate analytical needs into usable software tools and visualizations.
 - Presented technical findings at the annual AFSIM User Conference to an audience of researchers, engineers, and modeling-and-simulation professionals.
 - Transitioned from intern to full-time AI/ML Software Engineer after completing the internship.

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Conducted graduate research in natural-language processing, knowledge distillation, counterfactual learning, and explainable artificial intelligence.
 
 - Designed and evaluated a multitask knowledge-distillation framework for improving the robustness, efficiency, and interpretability of natural-language inference models.
 - Generated rationales and counterfactual training examples using a teacher large language model and distilled that supervision into smaller T5 student models.
 - Built reproducible data-processing, model-training, evaluation, and error-analysis pipelines using Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, and GPU computing.
 - Trained and compared T5 models across multiple parameter scales using standard fine-tuning, rationale distillation, naïve counterfactual distillation, and guided counterfactual distillation.
 - Evaluated model accuracy, macro F1, statistical significance, computational efficiency, counterfactual validity, and token-level label-changing behavior.
 - Presented research methods and findings to faculty and technical audiences and completed a peer-reviewed master’s thesis.
positions.insights: Skills: Amazon Web Services (AWS) · Natural Language Inference (NLI) · Hugging Face Transformers · Natural Language Processing (NLP) · Parallel Computing · Presentations · Problem Solving · OpenAI API · Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) · Interfaces · CUDA · Knowledge Distillation · PyTorch · Optimizing Performance · Reinforcement Learning

positions.title: .NET Development Bootcamp
positions.description:
Completed an intensive full-stack software-development program focused on object-oriented programming, web application development, relational databases, APIs, automated testing, and Agile delivery.
 
 - Developed full-stack applications using C#, .NET, ASP.NET, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and SQL.
 - Designed and consumed RESTful APIs and implemented data-access layers using relational databases.
 - Applied object-oriented design, unit testing, source control, debugging, and software-development best practices.
 - Collaborated on team-based capstone projects using Agile workflows, Git, and iterative delivery.
 - Completed the program before beginning formal undergraduate study in computer science.

projects.title: Leveraging Counterfactuals for Enhanced Natural-Language Inference: A Multitask Knowledge-Distillation Approach (MS Thesis)
projects.description:
Objective: Show that smart data beats sheer scale in Natural-Language Inference (NLI) by fine-tuning and distilling knowledge from a ChatGPT-4o-mini teacher LLM into smaller T5 student models.
Pipeline: Implemented four curricula—(1) Standard Fine-Tuning, (2) Rationale Distillation, (3) Naïve Counterfactual Distillation, and (4) Guided Counterfactual Distillation—across T5-Small/Base/Large/XL.
Data: Augmented ANLI Round 1 (16 k) and a 15 k slice of eSNLI with LLM-generated rationales + counterfactual hypotheses/explanations, yielding > 100 k multi-task targets.
Key Findings:
	•	On ANLI, Guided CF lifts T5-Small accuracy from 0.408 → 0.678 (+44 % error-rate reduction) and T5-Base from 0.492 → 0.729—outperforming a vanilla T5-Large at a fraction of the compute.
	•	A T5-Base + Guided CF run needed 29 GPU-hours vs. 47 GPU-hours for fine-tuned T5-XL, yet achieved higher accuracy.
	•	Counterfactual training delivers the biggest gains when parameters are scarce, enabling laptop-deployable LLMs for edge use-cases.
Impact: Provides a reproducible recipe for combining fine-tuning, knowledge distillation, and counterfactual reasoning to build robust, interpretable, and resource-efficient LLMs for NLI.
Key Skills & Technologies: PyTorch · Hugging Face Transformers · OpenAI API · LLM Fine-Tuning · LLM Knowledge Distillation · Counterfactual Data Augmentation · Natural-Language Inference · SLURM HPC · CUD · GitHub CI/CD · AWS HPC

projects.title: Machine Learning-based Simulation Software Analysis
projects.description:
Technologies Used: AFSIM, COSMOS, Galaxy, Dakota, Python, Bash scripting
Project Overview: Engaged in a detailed comparative analysis using machine learning to discern the application strengths of Leidos's proprietary software and the Air Force’s AFSIM scientific software, whilst adhering to strict confidentiality and security protocols.
Responsibilities and Achievements:
•	Designed and implemented machine learning algorithms for a side-by-side analytical comparison, ensuring accurate, unbiased results without exposing sensitive or proprietary data.
•	Facilitated strategic decision-making by providing key insights into the optimal utilization of scientific tools in varied situations, safeguarding resource allocation and efficacy.
•	Presented findings at the annual AFSIM User’s Conference, communicating complex data and insights effectively to a professional audience, and fostering a knowledge-sharing environment among experts in the field.
